rows.quote: For the primary analysis, we retrieved GWAS summary statistics for sepsis (ICD-10 code: A41) from the FinnGen consortium (Round 9), including 12,301 sepsis cases and 332,343 controls of European descent.[16] As external validation, we obtained independent GWAS data from the UK Biobank (2811 cases and 406,150 controls).[17] All datasets used were publicly available and approved for secondary analysis; therefore, no additional ethical approval was required.
rows.coder_note: 'the FinnGen consortium (Round 9)' is release 9 in another written form (rule A); the endpoint case and control counts are not a release N and no other identifier conflicts.

'GWAS data from the UK Biobank (2811 cases and 406,150 controls)' with ref 17, the Sudlow 2015 cohort description: exact counts with a cohort name alone, no accession, pipeline or GWAS citation (rule I1; a general cohort citation identifies no release).

rows.quote: To validate findings, we extracted additional pQTL data from the Fenland Study, which includes measurements of 4775 proteins in 10,708 individuals of European ancestry.[15] The same filtering criteria were applied.
rows.reference_quote: Pietzner M Wheeler E Carrasco-Zanini J . Mapping the proteo-genomic convergence of human diseases. Science . 2021 ; 374 : eabj1541 . 34648354 10.1126/science.abj1541 PMC9904207
rows.coder_note: The Fenland pQTL data are attributed to ref 15 (Pietzner 2021, DOI 10.1126/science.abj1541), the source of exactly one dictionary row; 4775 proteins in 10,708 individuals agree with it.

UKB-PPP is attributed to ref 11 (Sun 2023, DOI 10.1038/s41586-023-06592-6), whose source has several dictionary rows; the passages give 54,219 participants, Olink and 2923 proteins, none of which matches exactly one row (no subcohort or release-specific N), so rule E is not met.
